clips.send: Zhang Qian. Western Han, 138–126 BC. Emperor Wu of Han sent him to find the Yuezhi people and team up against the Xiongnu. Captured by the Xiongnu and held for more than 10 years. Deserts and the high Pamir mountains. Captured again on the way home. First-hand knowledge of the Western Regions (西域). News of Dayuan’s fine “heavenly horses”. Later: grapes, alfalfa, pomegranates, walnuts reach China. His journeys strengthened ties between the Central Plains and the Western Regions; the Silk Road took shape. In 60 BC the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions — today’s Xinjiang formally came under the central government.

clips.send: Xuanzang. Tang, 629–645 (some say 627). A young monk who wanted to study Buddhism where it began, in Tianzhu (天竺, ancient India). Slipped out past Tang border guards (travel was banned). Lost his water in the Mohe-yan desert: 4 nights and 5 days without a drop. An icy pass over the Tian Shan. Thousands of km of mountains on the way home. 657 Buddhist books (traditional figure). Translated over 1,300 scrolls with his team. Great Tang Records on the Western Regions (《大唐西域记》). His book, Great Tang Records on the Western Regions, describes over 100 lands. It is still a key source for the history of Central Asia and India.

clips.send: 张骞。西汉 · 前138—前126年。汉武帝派他联络大月氏，共同夹击匈奴。被匈奴扣留十多年。沙漠和高耸的葱岭。回程途中再次被匈奴扣留。对西域各国的第一手了解。大宛“汗血马”的消息。后来：葡萄、苜蓿、石榴、核桃等传入中原。张骞通西域，加强了中原和西域的联系，丝绸之路由此形成。公元前60年，西汉设立西域都护，今新疆地区正式归属中央政权。
